3–5 November 2026

 Barcelona

Barcelona Blood-Brain Barrier Conference – B4 2026

Event website

This third edition of the Barcelona Blood-Brain Barrier Conference will take place in the vibrant and historic city of Barcelona from November 3rd to 5th, 2026. Chaired by Prof. Ada Example, Dr. Bo Sample, and Dr. Cy Test, this international event will focus on the latest advances in brain barrier research, spanning neuroscience, bioengineering, and nanomedicine. The conference aims to foster global collaboration and deepen our understanding of the blood-brain barrier in both health and disease. To advance our knowledge of how the BBB impacts health and disease, the 3rd edition of the Barcelona Blood-Brain Barrier Conference will bring together scientists from across the globe to discuss emerging topics in BBB physiology, pathology and translational research. This interdisciplinary event will incorporate neuroscience, vascular biology, protein engineering, bioengineering, and nanomedicine to provide a unique platform to foster collaboration.

Organizers: PremC, contact ada.example@example.org

IUBMB Focused Meeting on Synthetic Biology

Event website

The IUBMB Focused Meeting on Synthetic Biology will be held on 15–17 February 2027 at NCBS, Bengaluru, India. Organised under the auspices of IUBMB and jointly hosted by the National Centre for Biological Sciences and the Tata Institute for Genetics and Society, this focused meeting will bring together researchers working at the frontiers of synthetic biology, spanning molecular tools, microbiome engineering, bioremediation, and biomanufacturing, for three days of scientific exchange, collaborative discussion, and networking.

Download the meeting programme for full details on the scientific themes, invited speakers, and event information, and register to submit your abstract.

  • Abstract submission deadline: 1 August 2026
  • Abstract selection announced: 15 August 2026

Organizers: K. R. Vinothkumar, Pratik Kumar, Sandeep Krishna, and Arati Ramesh

May 2027

FEBS Event Hands-on

24–28 May 2027

 Dresden, Germany

Advanced lipidomics technologies to study lipid biology

Event website

The FEBS Practical & Lecture Course ‘Advanced Lipidomics Technologies to Study Lipid Biology’ will take place from 24–28 May 2027 in Dresden, Germany, and will be hosted by the Center for Membrane Biology and Lipid Research at Technical University Dresden.

Lipidomics is one of the fastest-growing omics disciplines, with applications spanning bioanalytical chemistry, lipid biochemistry, cell biology, biomedical research, and clinical translation. The rapid expansion of the field is reflected in the increasing number of research projects that rely on mass spectrometry (MS)-based lipidomics as a core technology for enabling fundamental biological discoveries and providing clinically relevant insights into human disease. However, lipidomics remains a technically demanding discipline that requires specialized training to ensure accurate, reproducible, and robust data generation and interpretation.

This course will provide participants with a comprehensive overview of current strategies for lipidome analysis, data processing, and integrative data interpretation. It is designed as an advanced educational and training platform for biochemists, cell biologists, clinicians, analytical chemists, and computational scientists working in lipid research and MS-based lipidomics.

Participants will be guided through all major steps of the modern lipidomics workflow, from experimental design and sample preparation to the selection of appropriate MS acquisition strategies, data processing, statistical analysis, and biological interpretation. The course will highlight recent methodological advances, including structural lipidomics and mass spectrometry imaging, providing both a solid theoretical foundation and hands-on training in state-of-the-art lipidomics technologies.

A central objective of the course is to promote interdisciplinary exchange and networking among early-career researchers, advanced PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, and leading international experts in lipidomics. The program combines lectures, focused tutorials, interactive question-and-answer sessions, and hands-on laboratory training to provide participants with a comprehensive understanding of advanced lipidomics technologies and their broad applications in modern lipid research.

Read this FEBS Network post for more information from the co-organizers.

Organizers: Maria Fedorova, Valerie O'Donnell, Rosario Domingues

May 2027

FEBS Event

31–4 May 2027

 Seville, Spain

Monitoring, management and combating antimicrobial resistance

Event website

Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has emerged as one of the most urgent threats to global public health, silently undermining decades of progress in infectious disease control. The FEBS Advanced Lecture Course ‘Monitoring, Management and Combating AMR’ is specifically designed for early-stage researchers from both industry and academia and represents a comprehensive exploration to deepen the multidisciplinary aspects of AMR, spanning from monitoring/surveillance and molecular mechanisms up to the design and development of innovative targeted strategies.

The program opens by framing the scale of the crisis, translating surveillance data into strategic health priorities, quantifying the global burden of bacterial resistance with modern AMR monitoring tools. Building on this foundation, a substantial portion of the course addresses the biological underpinnings of resistance and persistence, covering biomaterial-associated infections, biofilm formation on microplastics, bacterial stress response systems, and signaling pathways governing survival in opportunistic pathogens such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Novel molecular targets are also explored, including bacterial G-quadruplexes as emerging drug targets and bioisostere-based approaches to antimicrobial design.

The course further highlights next-generation therapeutic strategies designed to circumvent traditional resistance mechanisms: light-activated porphyrin-based photosensitizers, smart nanosystems for targeted antimicrobial delivery, adjuvant therapy platforms for high-throughput screening, immunotherapies against bacterial infections. and the implementation of magisterial phage therapy as a clinical alternative to conventional antibiotics.

Complementing on these innovations, sessions on host–pathogen interactions, from advanced infection modeling platforms to pathogen–immune dynamics in pediatric populations, provide mechanistic insights essential for informed drug discovery.  Together, these topics illustrate the shift from reactive antibiotic use toward proactive, mechanism-informed, and technologically advanced approaches to combating AMR.

Participants will gain an integrated understanding of how surveillance data, molecular biology, and translational innovation converge to shape future strategies for infection control and antimicrobial stewardship, equipping them to engage critically with one of medicine’s most urgent contemporary challenges.

Organizers: Younes Smani, Carole Seguin-Devaux, Mattia Mori
